definition_english: Governed by capricious fancy, ungrounded speculation, or idiosyncratic whims; regionally (Maine, US), stubborn.
definition_hindi: मनमौजी कल्पना, निराधार अटकलों अथवा विचित्र तरंगों से संचालित; क्षेत्रीय (मेन, अमेरिका) प्रयोग में हठी या ज़िद्दी।

etymology.root_language: Latin (via Middle English and Medieval Latin)
etymology.historical_development: Formed from notion + -al (Latin -ālis). Branched outward from 14th–16th-century scholastic abstraction into the pejorative sense 'full of whims, dealing in imaginary things' by 1791 (attested in Online Etymology Dictionary), alongside a dated/regional Maine (US) sense meaning 'stubborn' (recorded in English Wiktionary).

equivalence_mapping.usage_status: Directly attested in opened Hindwi Dictionary entry for notional; covers capricious/fanciful S5 sense but does not cover regional Maine 'stubborn' sub-sense
Orthographic variant directly attested in opened Shabdkosh entry for notional; colloquial/evaluative register
Directly attested in opened Shabdkosh (entry: notional) and Hindwi (entry: kaalpanik as imaginary, fictitious, utopian); broader than S5 whimsy

syntactic_patterns: gradable attributive modifier before personal or abstract nouns (notional schemes, notional person)
gradable predicative complement after copula (became more notional)

hindi.gender: Invariable (अविकारी); agreement carried by modified noun
hindi.number: Invariable (अविकारी); agreement carried by modified noun
hindi.case: Invariable across direct and oblique cases
hindi.adjective_agreement: Invariable (अविकारी / अपरिवर्तनीय); does not inflect for gender, number, or case
syntactic_patterns: attributive pre-nominal modifier before masculine or feminine nouns
predicative evaluative modifier in colloquial and journalistic Hindi

register_and_pragmatics.formality: Informal to semi-formal (dated or regional in English)
register_and_pragmatics.connotation: Negative or mildly critical; implies capricious fancy or lack of practical grounding (and stubbornness in Maine US regional usage)
cultural_nuances: Whereas technical senses S1–S4 require formal Tatsama adjectives or the loanword नोशनल, S5 maps naturally to the colloquial Perso-Arabic adjective ख़्याली / ख़याली or everyday काल्पनिक.
usage_restrictions: Do not use ख़्याली / ख़याली in technical S1–S4 legal, financial, administrative, or linguistic contexts.
Reject Shabdkosh's erroneous fault-finding glosses छिद्रान्वेषी, नुकताचीन, and अवगुण ढूंढ़नेवाला, which misrepresent S5.
Do not use नोशनल, कल्पित, आनुमानिक, अवधारणात्मक, or धारणात्मक for S5 fanciful or capricious usage.
No attested Hindi equivalent for the Maine (US) regional sub-sense ('stubborn') was established in the opened research sources.

linguistic_analysis.morphosyntax: English notional in S5 is a gradable qualitative adjective (more notional, most notional) occurring attributively and predicatively. Hindi ख़्याली / ख़याली (Perso-Arabic loan adjective) and काल्पनिक (Sanskrit tatsama, kalpanā + -ika with vṛddhi) are both invariable adjectives whose gender and number agreement fall on the modified head noun.
linguistic_analysis.orthographic_variation: Opened Hindi dictionaries record two Devanagari spellings for the same Perso-Arabic adjective: ख़्याली (Hindwi) and ख़याली (Shabdkosh).

conceptual_analysis.core_distinction: Captures capricious, fanciful, or ungrounded mental whims—and in Maine regional English, obstinacy—rather than formal philosophical propositions (S1), legally binding administrative reckonings (S2), stipulated financial benchmarks (S3), or semantic grammatical concord (S4).
conceptual_analysis.domain_boundary: Distinct from technical senses S1–S4 and from the countable espionage noun S6 (front company).

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Both convey ungrounded, imaginary, or fanciful qualities in general Hindi.
pairwise_comparison.difference: ख़्याली / ख़याली is colloquial and Perso-Arabic, carrying an immediate evaluative flavor of daydreaming, whimsy, or impracticality suited to S5; काल्पनिक is broader, spanning everyday 'imaginary/utopian' as well as formal administrative/tax uses (S2/S3).
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: High in general evaluative prose for S5; prefer ख़्याली / ख़याली when emphasizing whimsy or impracticality and avoid काल्पनिक where administrative or legal ambiguity could arise.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Minimal; both touch on non-actual mental constructs in dictionary listings.
pairwise_comparison.difference: ख़्याली expresses capricious fancy in colloquial evaluative Hindi, whereas कल्पित is a high Tatsama participial adjective denoting a deliberate analytical or contractual posit (S3/S2).
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Not interchangeable; कल्पित is inappropriate for S5 pejorative/whimsical usage.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: None; linked only because Shabdkosh erroneously lists fault-finding terms under notional.
pairwise_comparison.difference: ख़्याली captures fanciful/whimsical unreality (S5), whereas छिद्रान्वेषी ('fault-finding/hypercritical') is a documented dictionary error that distorts S5.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Not interchangeable; छिद्रान्वेषी must be rejected.
